<p class=\"muted\">Cùng một ý tưởng (mỗi: One idea (every element emits and absorbs its own colours) is used every day, from observatories to laboratories and street lamps.
<p>Với hầu hết thiên thể, ánh sáng gần n: For most celestial objects, light is almost the only “messenger” that brings information to Earth. Each dark line in a star's spectrum is the trace of an element in its outer gas; counting the lines and measuring their strength reveals what the star is made of and how hot it is.
<p>Năm 1868, khi quan sát nhật hoa trong: In 1868, while observing the solar corona during an eclipse, astronomers saw a yellow line at 587.6 nm that matched no known element. The new element was named helium (from the Greek helios, the Sun), and it was found on Earth only 27 years later.
<p>Khi nguồn sáng chuyển động, cả bộ vạc: When a light source moves, its whole set of lines shifts slightly (the Doppler effect): towards red if it is receding, towards blue if it is approaching. Such tiny shifts led in 1995 to the discovery of the first planet orbiting a Sun-like star.
<p class=\"src\">Nguồn: Fraknoi và cs. (: Sources: Fraknoi et al. (2022); Mayor & Queloz (1995)
<p>Mỗi màu pháo hoa là một phép thử ngọn: Each firework colour is a giant flame test. Strontium salts give red, barium green, copper blue and sodium yellow; mixing strontium with copper produces purple.
<p>Điều thú vị là phần lớn ánh sáng khôn: Interestingly, most of that light does not come from lone metal atoms but from small molecules formed in the flame, such as SrCl, SrOH, BaCl and CuCl. That is why firework makers often add a chlorine-rich ingredient to help these molecules form.
<p>Màu xanh lam là khó nhất: phân tử CuC: Blue is the hardest colour: the CuCl molecule breaks apart if the flame is too hot, so a good blue firework has to burn at a “just right” temperature.
<p>Năm 1860, khi soi ánh sáng ngọn lửa c: In 1860, passing the light of a mineral-water flame through a spectroscope, Bunsen and Kirchhoff saw two unfamiliar blue lines. They belonged to an unknown element: caesium (Latin caesius, sky blue). The following year they discovered rubidium through its dark red lines.
<p>Ngày nay, máy <b>ICP-OES</b> dùng pla: Today ICP-OES instruments use an argon plasma at about 6000–10000 K to excite a sample and measure the emission lines of dozens of elements at once. They can detect heavy metals at parts-per-billion levels, so they are used to check drinking water, soil and food.
<p class=\"src\">Nguồn: Kirchhoff &amp;: Sources: Kirchhoff & Bunsen (1860); Flowers et al. (2019)
<p>Đèn đường <b>sodium áp suất thấp</b>: Low-pressure sodium street lamps emit almost nothing but the yellow 589 nm doublet. They are among the most energy-efficient lamps, but under that single colour everything looks yellow or grey: you cannot tell a red car from a blue one.
<p>Trong <b>đèn huỳnh quang</b>, hơi thủ: In a fluorescent lamp, mercury vapour emits most strongly at 253.7 nm, in the invisible ultraviolet. A phosphor coating inside the tube absorbs that UV and re-emits visible light in a few blue, green and red regions that together look almost white. Neon lamps use neon gas, which gives a characteristic red-orange glow.

<div class=\"modal-head\"><h2 id=\"about: About Aurora-LAB
<p class=\"about-lead\">Học khoa học khô: Learning science is more than memorising laws, concepts and results that others have discovered. Above all, it is the process of learning to observe the world, ask questions, test hypotheses and find answers for yourself, step by step.
<p><b>Aurora-LAB</b> được xây dựng từ ti: Aurora-LAB is built on that idea of education: it turns phenomena that are hard to observe, processes at atomic scales or across vast regions of space, into visual experiences that learners can actively explore.
<p>Đây là phòng thí nghiệm ảo về ánh sán: It is a virtual laboratory on atomic light and the aurora, developed by the STEM & Experiential Learning in Astronomy Research Group – USAC Astronomy Club. Through interactive simulations, learners can change the energy of an electron, explore how particles interact with the atmosphere, observe the light given off by heated elements and see how spectra are formed.
<blockquote class=\"about-quote\">Thay v: Instead of only receiving a ready-made conclusion, you take part in the process that leads to it.
<p>Aurora-LAB tập trung vào ba nội dung: Aurora-LAB focuses on three closely connected topics, all opening up one of the most important ways humanity studies the universe: the study of light.
<div class=\"about-card\"><span class=\":
1Photon emission by atoms

What happens when an electron absorbs energy and moves to a higher level? Why, on returning to a lower level, does the atom emit photons of precise energies, creating characteristic spectral lines?

2The aurora and the glowing atmosphere

How do charged particles, energised by the solar wind, interact with atoms and molecules in the atmosphere? Why do altitude and atmospheric composition produce the different colours of the aurora?

3From flame to spectrum

What can the light of heated elements reveal about the composition of matter? How can a bright line in a spectrum become the signature that identifies an element?
<p>Ba nội dung này cùng hướng đến một ng: All three point to one basic principle: light carries information about the matter that emitted it or interacted with it. Every element has its own set of energy levels and its own spectral signature. By studying these signatures, scientists can determine the chemical composition, temperature and many physical properties of objects thousands or even millions of light-years away.
<p>Từ một thí nghiệm nhỏ về ánh sáng tro: From a small experiment with light in a classroom, learners can reach a research method that has opened the door to understanding stars, nebulae and distant galaxies.
<p>Chúng tôi tin rằng một trải nghiệm gi: We believe a meaningful science learning experience lies not only in how much knowledge learners receive, but also in the questions it raises and the ability to explore on their own that it builds.
<li><span aria-hidden=\"true\">🔍</span><:
• 🔍
    Learning by exploring: Learners do not just watch results; they change the conditions of an experiment, follow what changes and work out the link between cause and effect.
<li><span aria-hidden=\"true\">👁</span><:
• 👁
    Making the invisible visible: Atomic processes, radiation the eye cannot see and events hundreds of kilometres up in the atmosphere are recreated in simulation, making abstract ideas more approachable.
<li><span aria-hidden=\"true\">🔗</span><:

    Connecting theory and experiment: Physical concepts do not live apart in textbooks; they are placed in concrete situations to observe and test, so learners can link model, phenomenon and scientific explanation.
<li><span aria-hidden=\"true\">📐</span><:
• 📐
    Scientific accuracy as the foundation: Spectral data follow the NIST Atomic Spectra Database; auroral physics is checked against peer-reviewed work and material from the NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center (SWPC). The content is written to be easy to follow while respecting the science (see ).
<li><span aria-hidden=\"true\">🌏</span><:
• 🌏
    Widening access to science: Not every school has full spectroscopy equipment. By building a web-based simulation environment, Aurora-LAB hopes to lower barriers of equipment and conditions, giving school pupils, university students, teachers and astronomy enthusiasts more chances to explore.
<p>Aurora-LAB không đặt mục tiêu thay th: Aurora-LAB does not aim to replace real experiments or the role of teachers. Instead, it hopes to be a supporting environment where learners can freely observe, experiment and form questions of their own.
<p>Bởi lẽ, hiểu một hiện tượng không chỉ: For understanding a phenomenon is not only knowing how it happens, but also why it happens and how we can test that explanation.

Màu đỏ là màu “nóng”, nên ánh sáng đỏ ma: Red is a “hot” colour, so red light carries more energy than blue light.
Ngược lại: mỗi photon đỏ mang ít năng lư: The opposite: each red photon carries less energy than a blue or violet one. In astronomy, hotter stars look blue-white and cooler stars orange-red. “Red means hot” is only a convention of art and daily life.
Năm 1865, James Clerk Maxwell chỉ ra rằn: In 1865 James Clerk Maxwell showed that changing electric and magnetic fields can “feed” each other and travel as a wave. The calculated speed matched the measured speed of light, so he concluded that light is an electromagnetic wave. Around 1887–1888 Heinrich Hertz produced and detected electromagnetic waves in the laboratory, confirming the prediction.
Trong chân không, mọi sóng điện từ đi vớ: In a vacuum, every electromagnetic wave travels at the same speed $c = 299\,792\,458\ \mathrm{m/s}$ (an exact number, because the metre is defined from it). Wavelength $\lambda$ and frequency $f$ are related by $c = \lambda f$: the shorter the wavelength, the higher the frequency.
Photon: “gói” năng lượng ánh sáng: The photon: a “packet” of light energy
Năm 1900, Max Planck phải giả định năng: In 1900 Max Planck had to assume that light energy is exchanged in small portions $E = hf$ to explain the radiation of hot bodies. In 1905 Albert Einstein went further: light really consists of particles of energy, now called photons, and he used the idea to explain the photoelectric effect.
Kết hợp hai hệ thức trên: $E = hf = \\df: Combining the two relations: $E = hf = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$. With $hc \approx 1239.84\ \mathrm{eV\cdot nm}$ we get the quick rule $E\,(\mathrm{eV}) \approx \dfrac{1240}{\lambda\,(\mathrm{nm})}$. For example, the aurora’s green 557.7 nm photon carries $E \approx \dfrac{1240}{557.7} \approx 2.22\ \mathrm{eV}$.
Mắt người “đọc” màu như thế nào?: How does the human eye “read” colour?
Võng mạc có ba loại tế bào nón, mỗi loại: The retina has three kinds of cone cells, each most sensitive to one range of wavelengths (short, medium, long). The brain compares their signals to create the sensation of colour. So colour is the brain’s interpretation of wavelength; a wavelength itself has no “colour”.
Ban ngày, mắt nhạy nhất với ánh sáng kho: In daylight the eye is most sensitive near 555 nm (yellowish green); in the dark, when rod cells do most of the work, the peak shifts to about 507 nm. The 380–780 nm range is a common convention; at both ends the eye’s sensitivity drops very sharply.
Ánh sáng nhìn thấy chỉ là một khoảng rất: Visible light is only a very narrow slice of the electromagnetic spectrum. Towards longer wavelengths lie infrared, microwaves and radio waves; towards shorter ones, ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays.
Khí quyển chặn phần lớn tia gamma, tia X: The atmosphere blocks most gamma rays, X-rays and ultraviolet (the ozone layer strongly absorbs ultraviolet below about 300 nm). To observe the universe in these ranges, astronomers must put telescopes in space.

Mô hình Bohr và công thức của hydrogen: The Bohr model and the hydrogen formula
Năm 1913, Niels Bohr đề xuất rằng electr: In 1913 Niels Bohr proposed that the electron in hydrogen can only be at certain energy levels: $E_n = -\dfrac{13.6\ \mathrm{eV}}{n^2}$ with $n = 1, 2, 3, \dots$ The minus sign means the electron is “held” by the nucleus; pulling it infinitely far away costs energy.
Mô hình Bohr giải thích chính xác quang: The Bohr model explains hydrogen’s spectrum precisely but fails for atoms with many electrons. Quantum mechanics, developed later (from 1925–1926), describes every atom correctly and still gives the same energy formula for hydrogen.
Công thức Rydberg: tính mọi vạch của hyd: The Rydberg formula: every hydrogen line
Từ công thức năng lượng, bước sóng của p: From the energy formula, the wavelength of the photon when an electron moves between levels $n_2$ and $n_1$ ($n_2 > n_1$) is: $$\frac{1}{\lambda} = R_\infty\left(\frac{1}{n_1^2} - \frac{1}{n_2^2}\right),\qquad R_\infty \approx 1.097 \times 10^{7}\ \mathrm{m^{-1}}$$
Ví dụ với $n_1 = 2$, $n_2 = 3$: $\\dfrac: For example with $n_1 = 2$, $n_2 = 3$: $\dfrac{1}{\lambda} = R_\infty\left(\dfrac14 - \dfrac19\right)$, giving $\lambda \approx 656\ \mathrm{nm}$, the red Hα line. (More precise measurements differ slightly because the nucleus is not perfectly still and wavelengths in air are a little shorter than in vacuum.)
Khi photon đủ mạnh để bứt electron ra: When a photon is strong enough to free the electron
Năng lượng ion hóa của hydrogen ở trạng: The ionisation energy of ground-state hydrogen is about 13.6 eV, matching $\lambda \approx \dfrac{1240}{13.6} \approx 91.2\ \mathrm{nm}$ (the Lyman limit). Any shorter wavelength can ionise the atom, so below 91.2 nm hydrogen absorbs continuously, not just at separate lines.
Vì sao vạch phổ không mảnh tuyệt đối?: Why are spectral lines not infinitely thin?
Mỗi vạch thực ra có một độ rộng nhỏ. Hai: Every line has a small width. Two common causes: atoms move randomly with heat, so their light is slightly Doppler-shifted (hotter gas, broader line); and collisions between atoms disturb the energy levels (denser gas, broader line). By measuring line widths astronomers estimate the temperature and pressure in stellar atmospheres.

Electron quay quanh hạt nhân theo quỹ đạ: Electrons circle the nucleus in round orbits like planets around the Sun.
Đó là hình ảnh của mô hình Bohr, rất hữu: That is the picture of the Bohr model, very handy for visualising energy levels but not how things really are. In quantum mechanics an electron has no definite orbit; we only know the probability of finding it in each region around the nucleus (called an orbital). What remains true is that the electron’s energy can only take certain values.
Electron ở trạng thái kích thích được ba: How long does an electron stay excited?
Với phần lớn các chuyển mức “được phép”,: For most “allowed” transitions, the excited state lasts only a few to tens of nanoseconds (1 ns = a billionth of a second) before emitting a photon. For example, sodium’s 3p level, the source of the yellow 589 nm line, lives about 16 ns.
Cơ sở dữ liệu NIST ghi cho mỗi vạch một: The NIST database gives each line a transition probability (in s⁻¹) that tells how fast the transition happens. The larger the value, the sooner the state shines.
Không phải cặp mức nào cũng dễ dàng chuy: Not every pair of levels connects easily. Conservation laws (especially of angular momentum, since a photon carries some) set selection rules. Transitions that break the usual rules can still happen, but millions of times more slowly or more; their lines are called forbidden lines.
Hai màu chính của cực quang (557,7 nm và: The aurora’s two main colours (oxygen’s 557.7 nm and 630.0 nm) are both forbidden lines: the states that emit them live about 0.7 s and 110 s. They are hard to see in laboratories on Earth because collisions take the energy before the light can come out.
Khi electron tự rơi xuống và phát photon: When an electron drops by itself and emits a photon in a random direction, that is spontaneous emission, as in a flame or the aurora. In 1917 Einstein pointed out another route: a passing photon can “trigger” an excited atom to emit an identical photon (same wavelength, direction and phase). This stimulated emission is the principle of the laser.

Johannes Rydberg generalised it a few years later. Theodore Lyman (ultraviolet) and Friedrich Paschen (infrared) then found new series, just as the formula predicted. Only in 1913 did the Bohr model explain where the formulas come from.
Quanh các ngôi sao trẻ, rất nóng, tia tử: Around very hot young stars, ultraviolet light ionises hydrogen gas. When electrons recombine with protons they “climb down the ladder”, emitting many lines, with Hα 656.3 nm very strong. That is why images of emission nebulae such as the Orion Nebula (M42) often look pink-red.
Kính lọc Hα cũng được dùng để quan sát l: Hα filters are also used to observe the Sun’s chromosphere and prominences, structures that are almost invisible in white light.
Lyman α: vạch quan trọng nhưng phải lên: Lyman α: the most important line, visible only from space
Vạch Lyman α (121,6 nm) là vạch mạnh nhấ: Lyman α (121.6 nm) is hydrogen’s strongest line, but Earth’s atmosphere absorbs it, so only space telescopes can see it. For very distant galaxies the line is redshifted by the expansion of the universe, sometimes right into the visible range, helping astronomers measure their distance.

A dark line is only darker than its surroundings. The outer gas absorbs photons of exactly that wavelength and re-emits them in all directions, so much less of that light travels straight to us, but not zero.
Vạch Fraunhofer: bí ẩn trong ánh sáng Mặ: Fraunhofer lines: a mystery in sunlight
Năm 1814, Joseph von Fraunhofer dùng kín: In 1814 Joseph von Fraunhofer, using a spectroscope of his own making, recorded the positions of more than 500 dark lines in the solar spectrum. He labelled the strongest with letters, such as the D line in the yellow. Nearly half a century later Kirchhoff and Bunsen showed that D coincides exactly with sodium’s emission line, meaning the Sun’s atmosphere contains sodium.
Ba quy luật Kirchhoff, giải thích bằng n: Kirchhoff’s three laws, explained by atoms
Trong vật rắn hay khí rất đặc, các nguyê: In solids or very dense gases, atoms interact strongly and energy levels merge into continuous bands, so a hot object emits every wavelength. In a thin gas each atom stands almost alone, keeping its own set of levels, so it only emits or absorbs at specific wavelengths. An element’s emission and absorption lines coincide because both come from the same pairs of levels.
Màu sắc và nhiệt độ của ngôi sao: The colour and temperature of stars
Phần liên tục trong quang phổ một ngôi s: The continuous part of a star’s spectrum resembles the radiation of an ideal hot body (a blackbody). The brightest wavelength follows Wien’s law: $$\lambda_{\max} = \frac{b}{T},\qquad b \approx 2.898 \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{m\cdot K}$$
Với Mặt Trời, nhiệt độ bề mặt hiệu dụng: For the Sun, the effective surface temperature is about $T \approx 5772\ \mathrm{K}$, giving $\lambda_{\max} \approx 500\ \mathrm{nm}$. Hotter stars peak at shorter wavelengths and look blue-white; cooler stars look orange-red.
Năm 1925, Cecilia Payne phân tích quang: In 1925 Cecilia Payne analysed stellar spectra and showed that stars are made mostly of hydrogen and helium, contrary to the view of the time. Today this is basic knowledge: most ordinary matter in stars is hydrogen and helium, with other elements only a small fraction.

Mỗi chuyển mức điện tử vì thế luôn đi kè: Every electronic transition therefore comes with changes in vibration and rotation. Instead of one line we get very many lines packed together. The same bands appear in the spectra of many comet heads and give them their green colour.
Trong ngọn lửa, khí quyển các hành tinh: In flames, planetary atmospheres and cool stars, molecules can survive without breaking apart. Recognising their bands tells scientists which molecules are there and at what temperature, because the intensity pattern within a band depends on temperature.

Lực Lorentz và chuyển động xoắn ốc: The Lorentz force and spiral motion
Hạt mang điện $q$ chuyển động với vận tố: A particle of charge $q$ moving with velocity $\vec v$ in a magnetic field $\vec B$ feels the Lorentz force $\vec F = q\,\vec v \times \vec B$. The force is always perpendicular to the velocity, so it neither speeds up nor slows the particle, only bends its path. The result: the particle circles a field line while sliding along it, tracing a spiral.
Bán kính vòng xoắn là $r = \\dfrac{m v_\: The gyroradius is $r = \dfrac{m v_\perp}{|q|B}$. For a 1 keV electron in a field of about $5 \times 10^{-5}\ \mathrm{T}$ (roughly the field near the ground at the poles), it is only a few metres. So the electron is almost “tied” to the field line.
Khi hạt đi về phía cực, các đường sức ch: As a particle approaches the poles, the field lines converge and the field strengthens. A strengthening field can turn the particle back like a mirror, so many particles are “trapped”, bouncing between hemispheres. This is how the Van Allen radiation belts, discovered by the Explorer 1 satellite in 1958, hold their particles. Only particles moving nearly along the field line reach air dense enough to make an aurora.
Cực quang không xuất hiện ngay tại cực,: The aurora does not appear right at the pole but concentrates on an oval ring around each magnetic pole, the auroral oval. In normal conditions it lies at high geomagnetic latitudes (about 65–70°), over places such as northern Norway, Iceland, Alaska and northern Canada. The electrons behind bright discrete arcs are usually accelerated to a few thousand eV a few thousand kilometres up, before plunging into the atmosphere.

Chỉ số Kp (từ 0 đến 9) do các đài từ kế: The Kp index (0 to 9), measured by ground magnetometers, shows how disturbed Earth’s magnetic field is in each 3-hour period. NOAA uses it in its G1–G5 storm scale and in aurora forecasts.

The denser the air, the more frequent the collisions, and the longer a state has to wait, the easier it is to quench.
Trên cao (khoảng 200–300 km), không khí: High up (about 200–300 km) the air is so thin that atoms can wait 110 seconds: the red 630 nm line shines. Hạt mang điện không thể băng ngang đường: A charged particle cannot cross field lines. The Lorentz force makes it spiral along a field line, like a bead on a string. Earth’s field is roughly that of a bar magnet: the lines bunch together and plunge into the atmosphere around the two poles.
Gió Mặt Trời là dòng plasma thổi liên tụ: The solar wind is a stream of plasma flowing from the Sun, but Earth’s field blocks most of it, forming a protective “bubble” called the magnetosphere. When the field carried by the solar wind “links up” with Earth’s field, energy is fed into the magnetosphere and accelerates electrons already in the magnetosphere to a few thousand eV. These electrons slide down the field lines into the upper atmosphere and make it glow.
Electron gây cực quang chủ yếu đến từ từ: Auroral electrons come mainly from the magnetosphere, “energised” by the solar wind, rather than flying straight from the Sun. They pour down into two oval rings around the magnetic poles.
